title: Packages and exports
summary: Group source files into packages and expose capitalized names.
rules: Files in one directory normally share a package name.
An identifier starting with an uppercase letter is exported.
An executable uses package main and a parameterless main function.

title: Imports
summary: Import packages by path, optionally with a local alias.
rules: Imports are scoped to the source file.
Unused imports are compile errors; use a blank alias only for initialization side effects.

title: Variables and short declarations
summary: Declare typed or inferred variables; use := within functions.
syntax:
var name Type
var name = expression
name := expression
a, b := first, second
rules: Uninitialized variables have their type’s zero value.
Short declarations require at least one new non-blank variable in the same block.
Short declarations cannot appear at package scope.

title: Constants and iota
summary: Define compile-time values, optionally in a repeated declaration group.
rules: Constant expressions cannot call ordinary functions.
iota starts at zero in each const group and increments per declaration line.

title: Functions and multiple results
summary: Declare named functions, parameters, and zero or more results.
rules: Adjacent parameters of the same type can share a type annotation.
Return values must match the declared results.

title: Closures and variadic parameters
summary: Use function values that capture variables, and accept a trailing variable argument list.
rules: Closures share captured variables with their surrounding scope.
A variadic parameter must be last and is a slice inside the function.

title: If statements
summary: Branch on a Boolean expression, optionally with an initialization statement.
rules: The condition must be Boolean; parentheses are optional.
An initialization variable is visible throughout the if/else statement.

title: For loops
summary: Repeat with a three-part clause, a condition, or no condition.
rules: Go uses for for all loops.
The post statement cannot be a short declaration.
break exits the innermost loop; continue starts its next iteration.

title: Range loops
summary: Iterate over collections, strings, channels, integers, or iterator functions.
rules: A string yields byte offsets and runes; a map yields keys and values in unspecified order.
A channel yields received values until it closes.
Integer range requires Go 1.22+; iterator functions require Go 1.23+.

title: Switch statements
summary: Choose a matching case by value or by Boolean condition.
rules: Cases do not fall through automatically.
An omitted switch expression is true.
fallthrough transfers to the next expression-switch case without testing it.

title: Slices and append
summary: Use a variable-length view over an array.
syntax:
[]Type{values}
make([]Type, length, capacity)
slice[low:high]
append(slice, values...)
copy(destination, source)
rules: Slices share their backing arrays until allocation creates another.
append returns a slice that must be retained.
A nil slice has length and capacity zero.

title: Arrays
summary: Use fixed-size values whose length is part of their type.
rules: Assigning an array copies its elements.
Slicing an array creates a slice over its storage.

title: Maps and lookup
summary: Associate comparable keys with values.
syntax:
map[Key]Value{key: value}
make(map[Key]Value)
value, ok := table[key]
delete(table, key)
rules: Reading an absent key returns the value type’s zero value.
Writing to a nil map panics; initialize it first.
Map iteration order is unspecified.

title: Strings and runes
summary: Represent immutable bytes as strings and Unicode code points as runes.
syntax:
"interpreted\nstring"
`raw string`
'r'
[]byte(text)
[]rune(text)
rules: len(string) counts bytes rather than Unicode code points.
Range decodes UTF-8 runes with their byte offsets.

title: Pointers
summary: Refer to addressable values and dereference them.
syntax:
var pointer *Type
pointer = &value
*pointer = replacement
new(Type)
rules: The zero value of a pointer is nil.
Dereferencing nil panics.
Go does not support ordinary pointer arithmetic.

title: Structs and composite literals
summary: Group named fields into a value type.
rules: Exported fields start with uppercase letters.
Struct assignment copies the value, including any contained pointers or slices.

title: Methods and receivers
summary: Attach behavior to a defined receiver type.
syntax:
func (receiver Type) Method() Result { return value }
func (receiver *Type) Mutate() { }
rules: A receiver base type must be defined in the same package.
Pointer receivers can modify the original value.
The method set of *T includes methods with T and *T receivers.

title: Interfaces
summary: Describe behavior using method sets implemented implicitly.
rules: A type implements an ordinary interface by having its required methods.
An interface containing a typed nil pointer is not itself nil.
Constraint interfaces with type terms can only be used as constraints.

title: Type assertions and type switches
summary: Inspect the dynamic type held in an interface value.
rules: A failing one-result assertion panics.
The two-result form returns a zero value and false when it fails.

title: Generics and constraints
summary: Parameterize functions and types with constrained type parameters.
rules: Requires Go 1.18+.
any accepts all types; comparable permits equality comparisons.
A method cannot declare additional type parameters.

title: Error returns
summary: Report ordinary failures with an error result and test it explicitly.
rules: The built-in error interface has Error() string.
nil usually indicates success.
Wrap errors with fmt.Errorf and %w to preserve errors.Is/As inspection.

title: Deferred calls
summary: Schedule a call when the surrounding function returns.
syntax:
defer function(arguments)
defer func() { statements }()
rules: The function value and arguments are evaluated when defer executes.
Deferred calls run in reverse registration order.

title: Panic and recover
summary: Unwind a goroutine after an exceptional failure, optionally recovering in a deferred function.
rules: recover must be called directly by a deferred function to stop a panic.
Recovery cannot catch a panic in another goroutine.
Prefer error returns for expected failures.

title: Goroutines
summary: Start a function call concurrently in the same address space.
syntax:
go function(arguments)
go func() { statements }()
rules: Arguments are evaluated in the calling goroutine.
The program exits when main returns; other goroutines do not keep it alive.
Synchronize shared mutable state with channels or synchronization primitives.

title: Channels
summary: Communicate typed values between goroutines.
syntax:
make(chan Type)
make(chan Type, capacity)
channel <- value
value, ok := <-channel
close(channel)
chan<- Type
<-chan Type
rules: Unbuffered sends wait for a receiver.
Receiving from a closed and drained channel returns the zero value and false.
Sending to or closing a closed channel panics. Sending or receiving on a nil channel blocks.

title: Select statements
summary: Wait on channel operations with optional non-blocking fallback.
rules: If several operations are ready, one is chosen pseudo-randomly.
default runs only when no communication can proceed.
Without default, select blocks until a case can proceed.

title: Gin routing, binding and request context
summary: Declare routes, validate request bodies and propagate cancellation with explicit HTTP contracts.
syntax:
r := gin.New()
r.GET("/path/:name", handler)
r.POST("/path", handler)
err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&input)
c.Param("name")
c.Request.Context()
c.JSON(status, value)
rules: Gin 1.12.0 requires Go 1.25+. The fixture pins Go 1.26.5; default build features are used.
binding tags select validation rules; ShouldBindJSON returns decoding/validation errors without choosing the response.
gin.New has no default logger/recovery middleware; add them deliberately for an application.
Use the request context for downstream work; handlers must cooperate with cancellation.

title: Chi routers, parameters and middleware
summary: Compose net/http handlers with nested routes, path values and request context.
syntax:
r := chi.NewRouter()
r.Use(middleware)
r.Route("/prefix", func(r chi.Router) { r.Get("/{id}", handler) })
id := chi.URLParam(req, "id")
ctx := req.Context()
r.ServeHTTP(writer, req)
rules: Chi v5.5.0 requires Go 1.24+. Import github.com/go-chi/chi/v5; the fixture uses Go 1.26.5.
Handlers use http.ResponseWriter and *http.Request; URL parameters live in routing context.
Install middleware before routes; a middleware returns an http.Handler wrapping the next handler.
A route miss, method mismatch, invalid parameter and canceled operation have different contracts. Cancellation is cooperative.

title: Testify assertions and mocks
summary: Check results, require prerequisites and verify consumer-facing mock interactions.
syntax:
require.NoError(t, err)
assert.Equal(t, expected, actual)
assert.ErrorIs(t, err, target)
require.ErrorAs(t, err, &typedError)
m.On("Method", argument).Return(value, err).Once()
m.AssertExpectations(t)
rules: Testify 1.12.1 requires Go 1.17+; the shared fixture uses Go 1.26.5. Packages assert, require and mock need no build tags.
assert reports a failure and returns a boolean; require uses FailNow and must run in the testing goroutine.
Put runnable tests in _test.go files. Use subtests to isolate cases; require can stop one case without skipping its siblings.
Mock expectations verify interactions, not actual service behavior. Set explicit call counts and assert expectations; typed return values must match accessors.
